test_cases.title: IMU App Scheduled at 200 Hz
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a mock IMU library and a fake monotonic clock. Register the app on a TDM static schedule configured for 200 Hz.
procedure: Configure the TDM scheduler period to 5000 microseconds (200 Hz).
Advance the fake clock and dispatch the schedule for one second of simulated time.
Count the number of times the IMU app Execute() entry point was invoked during the run.
Record the timestamps of each invocation.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The IMU app Execute() is invoked exactly 200 times in one simulated second, with inter-invocation period of 5000 microseconds plus or minus the scheduler tolerance.

test_cases.title: Single Library Sample Read Per Cycle
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a mock IMU library that counts calls to its sample-read function. Initialize the app via its New() entry point.
procedure: Reset the mock IMU library call counter to zero.
Invoke the IMU app Execute() entry point exactly one time.
Read the mock IMU library sample-read call counter.
Repeat the Execute() invocation ten times and re-check the counter.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The mock IMU library sample-read function is called exactly once per Execute() invocation; counter equals 1 after one call and 10 after ten calls.

test_cases.title: IMU Sample Published on Software Bus
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a mock IMU library and a software bus instance with a recording subscriber on the IMU sample topic.
procedure: Program the mock IMU library to return a known sample (ax=1.0, ay=2.0, az=3.0, gx=0.1, gy=0.2, gz=0.3).
Invoke the IMU app Execute() entry point one time.
Inspect the recording subscriber's received-message queue.
Decode the published message and compare each accelerometer and gyroscope field to the programmed values.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Exactly one IMU message is published on the software bus per Execute() call, and its accelerometer and gyroscope fields equal the values returned by the mock library.

test_cases.title: Monotonic Microsecond Timestamp on Published Message
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a mock IMU library and a fake monotonic clock whose value is controllable in microseconds and a recording bus subscriber to capture published IMU messages.
procedure: Set the fake monotonic clock to 1000 microseconds and invoke Execute(); capture the published message timestamp.
Advance the fake monotonic clock to 6000 microseconds and invoke Execute(); capture the published message timestamp.
Advance the fake monotonic clock to 11000 microseconds and invoke Execute(); capture the published message timestamp.
Compare each captured timestamp to the fake clock value at the time of the corresponding Execute() call.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each published IMU message carries a timestamp equal to the fake clock value at Execute() entry, and timestamps are strictly monotonically non-decreasing across cycles.

test_cases.title: Pass-Through Sample Content - No Transformation
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a mock IMU library that returns a scripted sequence of distinct samples and a recording bus subscriber.
procedure: Program the mock library to return the sequence: sample A, sample B, sample C with arbitrary distinct field values.
Invoke the IMU app Execute() three consecutive times.
Capture the three published IMU messages from the recording subscriber.
Compare each published message's accelerometer and gyroscope fields byte-for-byte to the corresponding library sample (after axis-frame mapping only).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each published message's sample fields match the corresponding library sample exactly; no smoothing, integration, or value modification beyond the documented body-frame axis mapping is observed.

test_cases.title: Body-Frame Axis Convention X-Forward Y-Right Z-Down
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a mock IMU library that returns sensor-frame samples whose mapping to body frame is documented.
procedure: Program the mock library to return a sample with a unit vector along the sensor-frame X axis only.
Invoke Execute() and capture the published message's accelerometer vector.
Repeat with unit vectors along sensor-frame Y and Z axes, capturing each published vector.
Repeat the three unit-vector tests for the gyroscope channel.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Published accelerometer and gyroscope vectors match the documented X-forward, Y-right, Z-down body frame mapping for all six unit-vector inputs.

test_cases.title: IMU Health Status Published Each Cycle
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a mock IMU library that exposes a health status accessor and a recording subscriber on the IMU health topic.
procedure: Program the mock library to report a HEALTHY status.
Invoke Execute() five consecutive times.
Count the IMU health messages received by the subscriber and verify each carries the HEALTHY value.
Reprogram the mock library to report a DEGRADED status, invoke Execute() once, and verify the next published health message carries DEGRADED.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Exactly one IMU health message is published per Execute() call; the message value tracks the mock library's reported health on every cycle.

test_cases.title: Deterministic Output for Identical Inputs
test_cases.setup: Instantiate two independent IMU app instances, each with its own mock library and recording subscriber, configured with identical seeds and identical fake clocks.
procedure: Program both mock libraries with the same scripted sample sequence of 100 samples.
Drive both apps through 100 Execute() calls each, advancing fake clocks identically.
Capture all published IMU sample messages and IMU health messages from both subscribers.
Perform a byte-for-byte comparison of the two recorded message streams.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The two recorded message streams (samples and health) are byte-for-byte identical across all 100 cycles.

test_cases.title: Accelerometer Range Verification at +/-16 G
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a mock IMU library that exposes a configured accelerometer range accessor.
procedure: Program the mock library to report an accelerometer range of plus or minus 16 G and initialize the IMU app via New().
Capture the IMU app initialization status and any logged or published configuration verification result.
Reprogram the mock library to report a range of plus or minus 8 G and re-initialize a fresh IMU app instance.
Capture the resulting initialization status or fault report.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Initialization succeeds with no fault when range is +/-16 G; when the library reports any other range, New() (or app initialization) returns a non-success status code distinct from JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS, AND no IMU sample messages are published on the software bus during the test window.

test_cases.title: Gyroscope Range Verification at +/-2000 dps
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a mock IMU library that exposes a configured gyroscope range accessor.
procedure: Program the mock library to report a gyroscope range of plus or minus 2000 dps and initialize the IMU app via New().
Capture the IMU app initialization status and any logged or published configuration verification result.
Reprogram the mock library to report a range of plus or minus 500 dps and re-initialize a fresh IMU app instance.
Capture the resulting initialization status or fault report.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Initialization succeeds with no fault when range is +/-2000 dps; when the library reports any other range, New() (or app initialization) returns a non-success status code distinct from JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS, AND no IMU sample messages are published on the software bus during the test window.

test_cases.title: Sustained 200 Hz Sample Publication Over One Second
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app, a mock IMU library returning incrementing sequence numbers, the TDM scheduler at 200 Hz, and a recording subscriber on the IMU sample topic.
procedure: Reset the recording subscriber and start the TDM scheduler.
Advance the fake clock by one second of simulated time while running the scheduler.
Stop the scheduler and read the count of received IMU sample messages.
Verify the sequence numbers in the received messages form a contiguous run starting from the first scheduled sample.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Exactly 200 IMU sample messages are published in one simulated second with strictly contiguous sequence numbers and no gaps or duplicates.

test_cases.title: Timestamp Monotonic Increase Across Many Cycles
test_cases.setup: Instantiate the IMU app with a fake monotonic clock that advances by 5000 microseconds per Execute() call and a recording subscriber and a stubbed IMU library returning programmed sample values.
procedure: Invoke Execute() 1000 consecutive times, advancing the fake clock by 5000 microseconds before each call.
Collect the timestamp field from every published IMU sample message.
Verify each timestamp is strictly greater than the previous timestamp.
Verify the difference between consecutive timestamps equals 5000 microseconds for every pair.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All 1000 published timestamps are strictly monotonically increasing with consecutive deltas equal to 5000 microseconds.
